Avery/Peter — quick status and a few notes from compliance: 

1) SIG/CAIQ snapshot: attached is our current responses export and a short indicator column showing evidence readiness (green = evidence on file, amber = evidence narrative only, red = needs artifacts). See "sig-caiq-snapshot-answers.docx".
2) ISO->FedRAMP crosswalk: we maintain a maintained mapping; for this ask I've prepared the one-page crosswalk PDF and an editable spreadsheet ("acme-map-template.xlsx") that lists control owner and recommended sample windows. High-level points: 
  - We map ISO A.10 (Cryptography) to FedRAMP SC families; KMS artifacts are available for hosted customers but for private deployments we provide a different evidence set (customer-managed key attestations).
  - Log retention: standard production logs retained 90 days; for FedRAMP sample we can provide 180-day snapshots on request (note operational cost and extraction TTL).
  - Enclave snapshots: for on-prem/private we can schedule snapshot windows; hosted artifacts are exported from our snapshot pipeline once per month by default.
3) Controls to flag: 
  - Access reviews (ISO A.9): evidence is narrative + periodic spreadsheets; if the auditor requests user-level attestations we can extract CSVs for the sample window but need 48 hours lead.
  - Incident response correlation (ISO A.16): we have playbooks and two anonymized incident summaries; full PII-redacted artifacts require legal signoff.

Action items: 
• Avery: sending the one-pager + the two attachments to Peter by EOD Monday.
• Peter: confirm whether KPMG will accept redacted artifacts for initial gap analysis or needs full logs.
• Kimberly: please flag any items that require security-level approvals before sharing.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference

Peter — attaching the one-page crosswalk and the evidence checklist. A few operational clarifications so the audit scope is set correctly: 

• Evidence windows: we can provide a 180-day log snapshot compressed export; extraction lead time is 72 hours for hosted exports and 5 business days for private/on-prem environments.
• KMS attestations: for hosted accounts we provide HSM configuration screenshots, key rotation logs, and KMS policy snippets. For private deployments we provide configuration templates and customer KMS attestation forms (we cannot produce customer-managed key material).
• SIG/CAIQ questions: the attached snapshot marks items that will require additional artifacts. Notably: 
  - CAIQ Q2.4 (encryption in transit) — evidence: TLS config, cipher suites, and internal test results (we can provide).
  - CAIQ Q5.1 (access provisioning) — evidence: user access change logs; extraction requires a 48-hour request window.

I've redacted a couple of internal ticket IDs from the incident playbook exports to protect customer references; if KPMG needs full context we can route an NDA addendum.

Attachments: redwood-compliance-playbook-v2.pdf (one-page crosswalk embedded), acme-map-template.xlsx, sig-caiq-snapshot-answers.docx
